commands.review_summary:
The PR adds gateway-side silent pairing provenance/pruning plus a unified Control UI Nodes & devices inventory with grouping, cleanup, removal, token actions, and inline approvals.

PR surface: Source +817, Tests +846, Docs +34, Other +132. Total +1829 across 24 files.

target.title: fix(gateway): stop paired-device duplication and redesign the Nodes page
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the Control UI **Nodes** page becomes unusable on active gateways: every local CLI run, agent session, or node process with an ephemeral state directory mints a fresh device keypair and silently re-pairs as a brand-new device, so the paired-device list grows without bound (dozens of duplicate rows per machine, each holding an active operator/node token). The page also duplicated the same machines across two separate cards (Devices and Nodes), offered no way to remove or clean up entries from the UI, and hid node re-approval requests entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Two-part fix at the right boundaries:

- **Gateway**: paired-device records now carry approval provenance (`approvedVia: owner | silent | trusted-cidr | bootstrap`). When a same-host **local** pairing is silently auto-approved, the gateway retires older `silent`-approved records for the same client cluster (`clientId`/`clientMode`/display name) that are not currently connected and were not approved within the last minute (concurrent-handshake grace). Local clients share the gateway host, so the cluster key cannot match a different machine, and they re-pair silently by construction. Trusted-CIDR, owner, bootstrap, and pre-provenance records are never auto-pruned; interactive approvals stay sticky across later silent re-approvals. `device.pair.list` additionally reports per-record live connection state so clients can tell active pairings from stale ones (operator-only clients never appear in the node catalog).
- **Control UI**: the Devices and Nodes cards are replaced by one **Nodes & devices** inventory that joins `device.pair.list` with the merged `node.list` catalog — one entry per machine with connected/offline and role chips, last-seen, expandable tokens (rotate/revoke) and capabilities. Duplicate pairings of the same client collapse into an expandable group; **Clean up N stale** bulk-removes duplicates that are offline *and* auto-approved (so affected clients re-pair silently, without user action); every entry gets a **Remove** action (routed through `node.pair.remove` and/or `device.pair.remove` by role); node pairing re-approvals (`pending-approval` / `pending-reapproval`) now surface inline with Approve/Reject. All management flows reuse existing RPCs; the only response change is the additive `connected` field.

Non-goals: migrating the JSON pairing stores to SQLite (existing migration debt, unchanged shape) and any change to pairing security policy — silent/trusted-CIDR approval rules are untouched; this only manages record lifecycle after approval.

## User Impact

- The Nodes page shows one row per machine instead of hundreds of duplicate hash-named rows, with duplicates grouped and one-click cleanup.
- Stale silent local pairings (per-session CLI/agent identities) no longer accumulate: the gateway retires them automatically when a replacement pairs, which also revokes their orphaned operator tokens.
- Operators can finally remove paired devices/nodes and approve node re-approvals from the dashboard; previously this required the CLI. Operator-only clients (CLI, browsers) now show live connection state.

## Evidence

- New unit coverage: `src/infra/device-pairing-prune.test.ts` (provenance kinds, owner/legacy stickiness, cluster/connected/trusted-cidr/grace-window gating), `src/gateway/device-pairing-prune.test.ts` (both stores cleaned, invalidate/disconnect ordering, `node.pair.resolved` broadcast), `src/gateway/server-methods/devices.test.ts` (per-record `connected`), `ui/src/lib/nodes/inventory.test.ts` (join, grouping, primary selection, stale gating, removal routing), updated `ui/src/pages/nodes/view.devices.test.ts` (render + action wiring).
- Focused runs green (108 tests across the touched suites); `pnpm check:changed` delegated to Blacksmith Testbox green.
- Visual verification via `pnpm dev:ui:mock` (mock scenario now includes representative nodes/devices data): unified card with pending approval, grouped duplicate, connected/offline chips, token rows, cleanup button.
- Two Codex autoreview rounds accepted and fixed 7 findings (cross-machine cluster collision → prune restricted to same-host `silent` records; concurrent-handshake race → 60s approval grace window; over-broad bulk cleanup → gated to offline auto-approved duplicates with server-reported connectivity; legacy provenance downgrade → pre-provenance records stay protected; UI type drift; error swallowed by reload). One finding consciously rejected: excluding trusted-CIDR entries from the confirmed bulk sweep — per-entry removal has the identical property, recovery is automatic via the same CIDR auto-approve policy, and the sweep only touches offline auto-approved duplicates the admin explicitly confirmed.
